Subject: CareDirect — assurance appendix ask and SOC2 artifacts

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal asked me to follow up with the specific assurance items we need included in the MSA/order form before we can schedule procurement review:

- Standard SOC 2 acceptance language and timeframe for producing the most recent report (we've attached last year's SOC2 as a reference).
- Penetration test notification window + scope (we'd like to be able to run a vendor test with limited staging access; see CSV for proposed assertions).
- Audit/inspection cadence: our security team expects a clear evidence cadence and a statement on what artifacts Redwood will provide on request.
- Evidence delivery channels and contact (we need a named owner and an SLA for evidence responses).

Can you share a proposed redline for the assurance appendix and confirm whether Redwood will accept a SOC 2 report plus support artifacts (not raw logs) as primary evidence? Also let us know any constraints around pen-test staging access and whether 72 hours notice is workable.

Attachments: CareDirect_SOC2_2025.pdf (stub), requested-pen-test-assertions.csv (stub)

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like a draft by end of next week.

Best,
Julie Park

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Julie Park <julie.park@caredirect.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CareDirect — assurance appendix ask and SOC2 artifacts

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list and the attachments. Short answers up front:

- SOC 2: yes, Redwood accepts a current SOC 2 Type II report plus a short artifacts bundle (control descriptions, key configuration snapshots). We do not provide tenant logs; we provide scoped derivative artifacts and an enumerated evidence list.
- Pen test: we can support customer-directed pen tests in staging with ephemeral, scoped access. Our usual ask is 48 hours notice and a short technical point-of-contact. I can be flexible to 72 hours if needed — open to discuss.
- Evidence cadence: we typically commit to a 2-week evidence-response SLA for standard requests and 5 business days for high-priority items. For scheduled inspections we propose a 10-business-day lead time for coordinated evidence packages.

I've attached a preliminary redline with suggested language for the MSA appendix that narrows inspection rights, defines sampling bands, and specifies acceptable evidence types. Can the CareDirect legal team review the redline and flag any non-starters?

Next steps:
- I will loop in Legal and Security (cc'd) for final wording.
- If you confirm 72 hours vs 48 hours for pen-test notice, we'll bake that into the redline.
- We can schedule a 30-min call early next week to walk through the redline and the order form impact.

Attachment: redline-proposed-msa-appendix.docx (stub)

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-23T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — proposed MSA assurance language and negotiation posture

Team,

Looping you in on the CareDirect request (thread attached). They want SOC2 acceptance, a pen-test window, and an evidence cadence. I drafted a conservative redline (attached) — highlights and proposed negotiation posture below:

Proposed legal commitments (customer-facing):
- SOC 2: Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a bounded artifacts bundle on request. Language: "Customer may request Provider's latest SOC 2 Type II report and supporting control descriptions; Provider will respond within 10 business days and may redact vendor-specific operational details."

- Penetration testing: allow customer-directed tests only in our staging environment under an ephemeral access policy. Language: "Customer may coordinate a single vendor-led penetration test per 12-month period in Provider staging with technical scoping approved in writing. Provider requires 48 hours notice for scheduled tests and may require up to 5 business days for operational coordination. Provider will not permit testing that targets production environments without a separate commercial agreement."

- Audit/inspection / evidence cadence: commit to a 2-week SLA for routine evidence requests; provide an evidence manifest for scheduled inspections with 10 business days lead time. Language: "Provider will respond to standard evidence requests within 10 business days and to critical evidence requests within 5 business days; scheduled inspection packages will be delivered within the agreed inspection lead time."

Negotiation levers to preserve:
- Keep inspection rights bounded (sampled/limited) vs unlimited forensic access.
- Reserve rights to redact vendor operational details and sensitive telemetry.
- Offer a one-time extension to 72 hours notice for pen-tests if that unblocks procurement — but prefer 48 hours in the contract.

Ask: can Legal (Laura) confirm the redline language is defensible from a compliance viewpoint and Security (Karthik/Monica) confirm the operational feasibility (staging footprint, SOC2 artifact list, contact points)? I want to present a single consolidated redline to CareDirect instead of multiple rounds.

Attachment: redline-proposed-msa-appendix.docx

—Jonas

From: Julie Park <julie.park@caredirect.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@caredirect.io
Date: 2026-04-27T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CareDirect — assurance appendix ask and SOC2 artifacts

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft redline. We reviewed with Legal and InfoSec. Few points and acceptance notes:

- SOC2: Accept the "report + bounded artifacts" approach. Procurement requests a line that lists the minimum artifacts (control mappings, encryption-at-rest config snapshot, relevant control owner contact).

- Pen-test notice: CareDirect prefers 72 hours notice to align with our vendor scheduling. Accept Redwood's staging-only constraint and that production tests need a separate agreement.

- Evidence cadence: 10 business days for scheduled inspection packages is OK; we still expect 5 business days for prioritized artifact requests. Please include a named evidence owner and escalation contact in the Order Form.

If Redwood can update the redline to reflect: (1) explicit artifact list, (2) 72h notice for pen-tests, and (3) evidence owner/email in the Order Form, we can move this to procurement review. Once you send the updated redline I will route to procurement and legal.

We attached a short redline with our inline edits (separate file). If you can produce a final doc by Friday we can circulate to procurement next week.

Attachments: care-direct-redline-snippet.docx (stub)

Best,
Julie Park
Head of InfoSec, CareDirect
